classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the three-year depreciation multiplier, then subtract the sale value and divide by three using the unrounded original cost.

content.prompt: A company buys new company cars every three years. At the end of the three years, it offers them for sale to the employees on the assumption that they have depreciated at 30% p.a. The company is presently advertising some cars at $\$30000$ each.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What did each car cost the company originally, correct to the nearest thousand dollars?

answer.worked:
Each year the car retains 70% of its value.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Original cost}&=30000\div0.70^3\\\text{Original cost}&\approx\$87000\end{align*}$$

This is rounded to the nearest thousand dollars.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the average depreciation in dollars p.a., correct to the nearest hundred dollars, on each car over the three-year period?

answer.short:
$\$19200$ p.a.

Use the unrounded original cost, subtract the sale value and divide by three.
answer.worked:
Use the unrounded original cost from part a.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Average annual depreciation}&=\frac{30000\div0.70^3-30000}{3}\\\text{Average annual depreciation}&\approx\$19200\text{ p.a.}\end{align*}$$

This is rounded to the nearest hundred dollars.
